one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-11-16 to 2026-12-16. No BKNG earnings are scheduled: Q4 results and the 2027 outlook come in late February (src 3). The industry prints are done: Expedia (Nov 4) and Airbnb (Nov 5) both guided Q4 down, and Expedia fell 12% (src 10,12,13). Events inside the window: Thanksgiving and holiday-travel data, CoStar weekly hotel data (late-October U.S. RevPAR +9.7%, src 25), Middle East conflict headlines that move airfares and long-haul demand (src 17), and any news on AI agents booking travel (Google, Meta Muse; src 18,19). These can move OTAs several percent on a day, in both directions. After a -20% year and a post-print drift lower, there is no edge either way. So the ladder is a symmetric lognormal around $157.53 at monthly vol 39%/3.5 = 11.1%.

fair_value.method: Quarterly driver build (room nights x GB per room night x take rate, GAAP margin after SBC) gives FY2027 GAAP EPS $11.67 and FY2028 $13.50. Horizon NTM EPS of $12.65 x 14.3x NTM P/E (peer median 22.5x, shrunk toward the own 13.1x at k = 0.8, less 0.3x for regulatory overhang) = $180.89.

downside.story: P10: the Middle East conflict and high airfares last through 2027 and Europe softens (UN Tourism-type +1-2% demand, src 14,15), room nights run ~6% below base; ADR flat; AI agents (Google cart, Meta Muse; src 18,19) start to take an auction cut so take rate falls ~40 bp; investment and marketing deleverage take ~250 bp off margin; the market re-rates OTAs further toward 11x as disintermediation fears grow (src 24).

base.story: Room nights +5% a year after a +2.5% Q4 2026, ADR plus mix +2-3%, take rate down 10 bp in 2027 then flat, GAAP margin +30 bp a year, buybacks retire ~5.5% a year, and the P/E re-rates a little, from 13.1x to 14.3x.

upside.story: P90: travel normalizes in H1 2027 as the conflict effects fade, room nights grow ~8% (Q3 2026 pace plus easy comps), ADR and flight attach add 1.5%, payments lift take, full transformation savings drop through (+120 bp), and the AI-referral channel proves incremental (CFO: <1% of room nights, src 3), so the multiple recovers toward ~17x, still below the peer median.

sbc_treatment.note: FY2025 stock-based compensation $613M (10-K). The model uses GAAP EBIT after SBC, the share count falls only by net buybacks (-5.5%/yr), and peers' NTM P/E is on consensus EPS, which for EXPE/ABNB is adjusted. That basis mismatch slightly favors the peers (adds SBC back), so a strict SBC-costed peer median would sit lower; this is one more reason the multiple stays far below the median.

reasoning: Facts: Q3 2026 beat its own guide on every line (room nights +7%, adjusted revenue +9%, adj. EBITDA +9%; GAAP revenue -1% after a $900M FTC revenue reduction; src 1,3). But the CFO guided Q4 to room nights +1-3% and adjusted revenue +0-2%, citing October Middle East and European disruption (src 3). Industry lane: Expedia guided Q4 bookings down from +11% to +3-5% and fell 12%, with its CFO naming the same geopolitical headwinds (src 10,11,12). Airbnb accelerated (src 13), which shows that share in alternative accommodations is contested. UN Tourism cut 2026 arrivals growth to 1-2% (src 14,15). U.S. hotel ADR/RevPAR were firm in late October (src 25), and CoStar raised its 2026-27 outlook (src 16). AI agents: Google's partner list runs through the OTAs (src 18), but Meta Muse direct-booking fears hit the group in September (src 19,24). BKNG says LLM referrals are <1% of room nights (CFO, src 3). Build: four quarterly drivers. Room nights +2.5% in Q4 (inside the guide, below the record-adjusted 297.7M) and +5% in 2027-28. GB per room night +1-3%. Take rate -10 bp in 2027 on flight mix. GAAP margin +30 bp a year from transformation savings net of investment. FY2027 revenue $31.0B (1.5% below the $31.5B consensus) and GAAP EPS $11.67 (4.6% below the $12.23 adjusted consensus, src 9): moderately conservative per rule 0c. Value: one P/E leg; the exit 14.3x comes from the k = 0.8 shrink of the own 13.1x toward the 2-peer median of 22.5x, less 0.3x for regulation. Research target (12m) $180.89 (+14.8%). Downside P10 $116 (volume, take and margin cuts plus de-rating to ~11x) and upside P90 $234 give a fatter left tail, consistent with 39% realized vol and AI-disintermediation risk. Research was limited to web sources; the SEC blocked direct curl, so filings were read via WebFetch and companyfacts.

horizon_multiples.peer_basis: Median NTM P/E of EXPE (15.3x) and ABNB (29.7x) = 22.5x from peers.md; own NTM P/E 13.1x (157.53 / 12.00 NTM consensus EPS, src 9); shrink k = 0.8 gives 14.6x; less 0.3x for regulatory overhang (FTC, DMA) = 14.3x

inputs_detail.derivation: Q4 2026 152.4 (+1.0% y/y): CFO guide gross bookings +2-4% vs room nights +1-3% with FX -2 pts (src 3). FY2027 y/y +1.0% / +1.5% / +2.5% / +3.0%: constant-currency ADR +3% in Q3 (CFO, src 3), Expedia ADR +2% (src 10), U.S. weekly ADR +5.2% (CoStar src 25), plus flights and attractions mix (+19%/+24% tickets, src 3), less an FX drag in H1 2027 as the euro sits at $1.12 (CFO's assumption, src 3) vs H1 2026. FY2028 +3.0%: ADR +2% plus ~1 pt connected-trip mix. Alternatives: hold cc ADR at 0% (hotel pricing stalls, CoStar sees mid-2027 weakness, src 16): -2.5% revenue; or full +4% (Q3 2026 cc gap of 4 pts between GB and RN, src 3).
inputs_detail.variant_view: Zero ADR growth through 2027 lowers FY2027 revenue ~2% and the target ~3%.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q3 2026 actual 16.32% is GAAP after the $900M FTC revenue reduction (src 1,20); adjusted take 17.97% (9,793/54,500). Q4 2026 14.52% = Q4 2025 14.77% less 25 bp: guide adjusted revenue +0-2% vs gross bookings +2-4% because of flight mix and booking-vs-travel timing, partly offset by payments revenue (CFO, src 3). FY2027 each quarter = FY2026 adjusted same-quarter take less 10 bp (Q3 2026 ran -15 bp y/y on the same mix effects, CFO src 3; payments revenue grows with merchant mix at 75% of GB, src 3). FY2028 flat y/y: the CFO's long-term ambition is revenue growing with gross bookings (src 3). Seasonal shape is the stay-vs-booking timing; quarterly gross bookings were only collected for FY2025-26 (flag). Alternatives: -25 bp a year (agentic/AI channels or Google cart take an auction cut, src 18,19) or flat in 2027 (payments offset fully).
inputs_detail.variant_view: A 25 bp lower take each year (agent fees) cuts FY2028 revenue ~3.5% and the target ~5%.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2026 underlying same-quarter GAAP margins ex one-offs: Q1 21.0% (adj. EBITDA 1,290 - D&A 131 = 1,159 on 5,532; GAAP 23.0% had a ~$112M net gain excluded from adjusted), Q2 34.3% (2,648-129 on 7,352), Q3 45.1% ((3,418+1,000 FTC)/9,793), Q4 30.7% (guide adj. FY2028 another +30 bp. Alternatives: margin flat (investment absorbs the savings, as Expedia flagged moderating marketing leverage, src 11): about -3% target; or +100 bp (full savings drop through): about +3%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Flat margins vs +30 bp/yr: about -3% on the target.

Peer median 22.5x (EXPE 15.3x, ABNB 29.7x; peers.md). Own NTM P/E 13.1x = 157.53 / (0.125 x 10.42 FY2026 + 0.875 x 12.23 FY2027 consensus EPS = 12.00; src 9). Rule: 22.5 x (13.1/22.5)^0.8 = 14.6x; less 0.3x for the FTC and DMA regulatory overhang = 14.3x. Alternatives: k = 1 (own 13.1x) gives ~-8%; EXPE alone at today's price (13.0x, src 23) ~-9%; the rule's 14.6x +2%.

model_inputs.structure_note: Single-segment marketplace built quarterly from four drivers: room nights x gross bookings per room night x take rate = revenue (100% driven), and GAAP operating margin after SBC. The value is carried by one P/E leg on the model's own NTM GAAP EPS at the horizon (weight 1.0). No DCF (policy). No SOTP, because BKNG does not report segments (a combined B2B unit starts 2027-01-01, CFO src 3).
model_inputs.gap_note: Flags for Kilian: (1) Peer set is 2 names (EXPE, ABNB); median 22.5x is sensitive to ABNB. (2) The take-rate quarterly shape uses only FY2025-26 quarterly gross bookings. (3) The FTC $900M revenue reduction and $100M accrual sit in the Q3 2026 actuals. Whether any further cash payment or ongoing fee or disclosure change follows is not disclosed (10-Q note 13 not read in detail): probability <20%, so it is not modeled. (4) Exit multiple 14.3x vs today's 13.1x: k = 1 would cut the target ~8% (>5%: card). (5) The EPS basis is GAAP. Consensus is adjusted EPS, and in a normal year the gap is small.
